q: There is Myanmar riddle 'Which is heavier, a viss of cotton (or) a viss of ____ ?'
e: This riddle introduces the concept of density, as a viss of both has the same mass but different volumes.

q: Density is the ratio of ____ to volume of a substance.
e: Density is defined as the amount of mass per unit volume of a given substance.

q: Density is the ratio of mass to ____ of a substance.
e: Density is calculated by dividing the mass of a substance by its volume.

q: Density is the ____ quantity.
e: Density has magnitude but no direction, classifying it as a scalar quantity.

q: The Greek alphabet used to represent density is ____.
e: The Greek letter rho ($\rho$) is the standard symbol used to denote density in physics.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in ____ ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$).
e: The standard SI unit for density is kilograms per cubic metre.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre (____).
e: The symbol for the SI unit of density is kg m$^{-3}$.

q: In CGS unit, it is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per ____ ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$).
e: In the CGS system, density can also be expressed as grams per millilitre, which is equivalent to grams per cubic centimetre.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a ____ and volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder.
e: A balance is the standard laboratory instrument used to measure the mass of an object.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a balance and volume can be measured using a ____.
e: A measuring cylinder is commonly used to determine the volume of liquids or irregular solids via displacement.

q: Mass of the object does not change, but the ____ depends on the temperature.
e: While mass remains constant, the volume of a substance can expand or contract with changes in temperature.

q: If the volume changes, the ____ will change.
e: Since density is mass divided by volume, any change in volume (with constant mass) results in a change in density.

q: Average density of a human body is a little less than ____ density.
e: The human body's average density is slightly less than that of water, which is why humans can float.

q: The density of water at 4°C is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Water reaches its maximum density of 1000 kg m$^{-3}$ at a temperature of 4°C.

q: The density of aluminium is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Aluminium has a relatively low density of 2700 kg m$^{-3}$, making it useful for lightweight structures.

q: The density of copper is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Copper is a dense metal with a density of 8900 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of lead is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Lead is a very dense metal, with a density of 11400 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of mercury is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature with a high density of 13600 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of gold is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Gold is a very dense precious metal, with a density of 19300 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of uranium is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Uranium is a heavy metal with a density of 19050 kg m$^{-3}$.
